bull.b: Strong revenue, gross-profit and adjusted EBITDA growth demonstrates improved operating scale and earnings capacity. Although higher gold prices were a major driver, the wider margins and EBITDA expansion provide a stronger base for funding operations and development over the next several quarters.

The expanded How Mine mill can materially increase throughput once commissioning and ramp-up are complete. Higher processing capacity creates a structural opportunity to lift production from existing operations, improve fixed-cost absorption, and support stronger revenue generation into 2027.

Improving operating cash generation strengthens the company’s ability to fund mine development and meet obligations from internal operations. Management’s stated plan to reinvest this cash into the business also supports production growth, although the benefits depend on disciplined capital deployment.

bear.b: Persistently negative equity is a durable capital-structure weakness that reduces the company’s financial flexibility and increases vulnerability if operating performance deteriorates. It can constrain access to funding, complicate future investment decisions, and make balance-sheet repair an important long-term priority.

The large working-capital deficit places ongoing pressure on liquidity and requires dependable operating cash flow, financing access, or asset-level cash generation. Short-term borrowings and purchase commitments add to the funding burden, leaving less flexibility if production or cash receipts disappoint.

bear.t: Lower production and higher cost guidance
bear.b: Reduced production guidance and higher all-in sustaining costs indicate execution and cost pressures that can weaken cash generation and margins. The delayed mill ramp, lower grades, and fewer ounces leave the business more dependent on favorable operating performance and gold prices to achieve its plans.
